adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents()` now loops over each destination calendar, selecting a credential per destination and calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` (packages/core/EventManager.ts). However non-Google calendar services still derive the target calendar from only the first element: Lark (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`), O365 (same pattern), and BaseCalendarService filters by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (packages/app-store/larkcalendar..., office365calendar..., packages/lib/CalendarService.ts). Since `CalendarManager.createEvent()` always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` but these services don't use credentialId to pick the matching destination calendar entry, a later host's credential can be used while still targeting `destinationCalendar[0]` (host A), which can cause API errors and missing events for other hosts in collective/multi-host scenarios.
